summary: Opening an existing chat on any client shows the provider, profile and runtime mode the backend stores for it. The history load reads them from the root conversation, so a chat opened by its rotated session id no longer reads the empty settings of its own row, and both phones show the stored profile instead of the first profile or a saved copy.

storageDataMigration.reason: No schema change. The settings already live on the root conversation row and the setters already resolve through resolveRootThreadId; only the history load read the wrong row.

updateRelease.notes: The wire shape of the history meta is unchanged, so an old phone gets correct values from a new backend, and a new phone works against an old backend. The Expo change is JS only (OTA lane); Android ships in the next Play build.

automated: tests/unit/chat-load-rotated-settings.test.ts: a chat opened by its rotated id loads the root row's profile, mode, model and effort, and a change written through the rotated id shows on the next load by either id. Both cases failed before the fix (null profile and mode).

apps/mobile thread-stored-settings.test.tsx renders ThreadScreen against the demo transport with a stored Work profile and Plan mode: the chip shows Work, not the first profile, and a mode picked on the phone goes to provider:set-runtime-mode, which stores it. The profile case failed before the fix.

ThreadSessionCoordinatorTest: a saved copy with another profile is replaced by the loaded profile and mode, the reattach starts on the stored profile, and a profile change sends it as the expected current profile. It failed before the fix.
notExercised: Not run on a phone or against a live desktop. The fix was checked with unit and screen tests only.
A mode picked offline on Android is still kept over the loaded mode until a turn carries it. This is the existing, tested design for picks the backend has not seen.
